openTomorrow: Yes, absolutely. I want to log my morning run tomorrow and track my distance. It's become part of my routine now.
secured: I think it means my data is protected and private, like my run records are safely stored and encrypted so only I can see them.
freeze: I'm guessing it means I can pause or temporarily stop a challenge without losing progress, in case I need a break from tracking.
selfReported: It means I manually enter my run data myself instead of it being automatically tracked by my watch or GPS app.
best: Seeing my distance achievements displayed clearly. It's motivating to watch my mileage add up and compare it week to week.
worst: The interface felt a bit cluttered with all these different categories - Fitness, Faith, Mind, Health. I just want to focus on my running, and it took me a minute to find where my Run task was.
tellFriend: Yes, definitely. I'd say: 'It's a solid app if you're into fitness tracking, especially running. You can log your distances and see your progress over time. Just note that it groups a lot of different wellness stuff together, so you might need to dig a bit to find what you need.'
